items.title: Decide the authoritative dev_start phase set and align command-policy.ts + config.ts so they agree
items.context: Examine dev_start's real recovery semantics in handlers/worktree.ts (what it does in each of INIT/INIT_CHECK/PLAN/DEV, and whether standalone invocation is meaningful/safe in INIT and DEV). Per the PLAN decision, either add dev_start to DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS for the missing phases (widen config up to command-policy's ['INIT','INIT_CHECK','PLAN','DEV']) or shrink command-policy allowedPhases to match config (['INIT_CHECK','PLAN']). Update whichever source moves so command-policy.allowedPhases and the isCommandAllowed view derived from DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS agree for dev_start. Do NOT change dev_start behavior, the bootstrap flow, or REVIEW/TEST/DONE refusal.
items.userSees: npm run test:process-fact-contract no longer reports a dev_start INIT or DEV policy/default phase drift; command-policy.allowedPhases and DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS agree on dev_start's phases.

happy.desc: After adding the literal dev_start to DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS INIT and DEV, command-policy.allowedPhases and the isCommandAllowed-from-config view agree for dev_start across all phases

edge.desc: Only dev_start's phase permissions change; no other command shifts (exact literal added, not a wildcard) — contract reverse-direction check still holds

adversarial.desc: command-policy.ts and the handler's allowedPhases for dev_start are unchanged (config moves to match them); dev_start remains refused in REVIEW/TEST/DONE

verificationEvidence.note: After adding dev_start to DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS INIT+DEV, the contract assertCommandPolicyPhaseAlignment passes (command-policy.allowedPhases === isCommandAllowed for dev_start across all phases); contract exit 0
git diff shows ONLY config.ts with 2 insertions (the two literal dev_start lines); no other command or phase changed
command-policy.ts and worktree.ts have ZERO diff vs main (config aligned up to them, not vice versa); dev_start still refused in REVIEW/TEST/DONE (allowedPhases unchanged at the 4 pre-REVIEW phases)

items.title: Regression guard: npm run test:process-fact-contract passes and a future dev_start phase divergence is caught
items.context: Confirm npm run test:process-fact-contract exits 0 after the alignment. Ensure the contract check (or an added focused assertion) would fail again if command-policy.allowedPhases and DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS diverge for dev_start in the future, so the fix is mechanically protected rather than by convention. If the existing verify-process-fact-contract.mjs already covers this once aligned, record that it is the guard; do not add a redundant test.
items.userSees: npm run test:process-fact-contract exits 0; re-introducing the INIT/DEV mismatch (locally) turns it red again, proving the divergence is mechanically caught.

happy.desc: npm run test:process-fact-contract exits 0 (no dev_start INIT/DEV drift) after the alignment

edge.desc: The existing assertCommandPolicyPhaseAlignment in verify-process-fact-contract.mjs is confirmed as the guard; no redundant test added

adversarial.desc: Re-introducing the INIT/DEV mismatch locally turns the contract red again (exit 1), proving the divergence is mechanically caught

verificationEvidence.note: npm run test:process-fact-contract exits 0 after the alignment (no dev_start INIT/DEV drift, no new drift surfaced)
The existing assertCommandPolicyPhaseAlignment in verify-process-fact-contract.mjs is the guard (asserts policy<->config agree for every command x phase, both directions); no redundant test added
Round-trip proof: removing dev_start from the DEV array turns the contract RED (exit 1, dev_start DEV policy/default phase drift); restoring it returns exit 0 — divergence is mechanically caught
